corrected_fields.summary: Federal Reserve document summarizing responses to proposed 2026 supervisory stress test scenarios. Covers baseline scenario variables (unemployment, GDP, CPI inflation, Treasury yields, mortgage rates, equity prices, VIX, house prices, commercial real estate prices) and severely adverse scenario conditions. Documents changes made to scenarios based on 5 comments received. Used consensus forecasts from Blue Chip Financial Forecasts (August 29, 2025) and Blue Chip Economic Indicators (August 11, 2025) for baseline projections.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: Supervisory stress tests affect bank capital requirements and risk management frameworks. The scenario parameters (yields, spreads, equity shocks, VIX levels) directly impact how banks model potential losses and maintain capital buffers. Changes to these scenarios affect market expectations for bank regulatory burden and capital distribution capacity.
corrected_fields.macro_context: Fed conducts annual supervisory stress tests under DFAST (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing). The 2026 scenarios are used to evaluate bank resilience to adverse economic conditions. Baseline scenario aligned with consensus economic forecasts. Severely adverse scenario provides more extreme stress conditions for reverse stress testing.
corrected_fields.market_structure_context: Stress test scenarios directly influence: (1) Treasury yield curves used for valuation and duration sensitivity modeling, (2) Credit spread assumptions for bond portfolios (BBB yields, spreads), (3) Equity price shocks affecting market cap and VaR calculations, (4) VIX levels used in options and derivatives pricing, (5) CRE price assumptions affecting commercial mortgage portfolio valuations, (6) Interest rate sensitivity for asset-liability management.
